info.name: Velaris - API Documentation
info.description:
Base URL: https://api.euw1.velaris.io

Authentication

Velaris API can be authenticated via two options which are Basic Authentication and Token based Authentication.

Token based authentication

Using token based authentication, any user can create a Velaris API token that is specific for a user and use it. It is applicable for both single sign on enabled tenants and others.

Using the following steps, a token can be generated.

  • Step 1: Login to your Velaris application

  • Step 2: Click on the profile icon and then navigate to Security

  • Step 3: Under the Access token section you can find the button to create/view token.

Generated access token can be used in the headers in the following manner.
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}

Basic authentication (Legacy method)

For basic authentication, you will be using your username and password that are used to login to Velaris. Please note that it will not work for the tenants who have enabled single sign on.

You can generate a basic authentication token using following steps.

  • Step 1: Obtain username and password of a velaris user with administrator privileges

  • Step 2: Generate this token string in the following format username:password.

  • Step 3: Run Base64 encoding for above string. Use the result string as the generated_token

Generated authentication token should be passed in headers.

Authorization: Basic {generated_token}

Note: Please note that you will have to use the 'Token based authentication' if you have SSO enabled or multi factor authentication enabled.

Please note that the token has exactly the same permission as the user who have created the token.

response.name: Get All Organizations

request.description:
Search organizations using custom attributes

The request body should contain a list of filters up to 5 filters

  • filters - list of filters

    • filter - object

      • fieldName: API name of the custom attribute

      • operator: operator which should be used in the filter

      • value: filtered value

Supported Operators

Data type Operators
String equals, contains
Number equals, greaterThan, lessThan, greaterThanOrEqualTo, lessThanOrEqualTo
Date equals, after, before, onOrAfter, onOrBefore
Boolean equals
Single Picklist equals
Multi Picklist includes
Organization / Account / Contact / User Picklist includes

Valid Format of the value

  • String: Value must be a non-empty string.

  • Number: Value must be a valid number (can be provided as a string).

  • Date: Value must be a date string in the format "YYYY-MM-DD".

  • Boolean: Value must be a boolean string ('true' or 'false').

  • Multi Picklist, Organization Picklist, Account Picklist, Contact Picklist, User Picklist: Value must be a non-empty array of numbers.

request.description:
Search contacts using custom attributes

The request body should contain a list of filters up to 5 filters

  • filters - list of filters

    • filter - object

      • fieldName: API name of the custom attribute

      • operator: operator which should be used in the filter

      • value: filtered value

Supported Operators

Data type Operators
String equals, contains
Number equals, greaterThan, lessThan, greaterThanOrEqualTo, lessThanOrEqualTo
Date equals, after, before, onOrAfter, onOrBefore
Boolean equals
Single Picklist equals
Multi Picklist includes
Organization / Account / Contact / User Picklist includes

Valid Format of the value

  • String: Value must be a non-empty string.

  • Number: Value must be a valid number (can be provided as a string).

  • Date: Value must be a date string in the format "YYYY-MM-DD".

  • Boolean: Value must be a boolean string ('true' or 'false').

  • Multi Picklist, Organization Picklist, Account Picklist, Contact Picklist, User Picklist: Value must be a non-empty array of numbers.
